what: Coinbase is the largest cryptocurrency exchange in the United States. People and institutions buy, sell and hold crypto assets there, and it has been expanding into stock trading, stablecoins and derivatives.
customers: Retail crypto traders, institutional investors, and companies building on its infrastructure.
money: trading fees from retail and institutional customers
custody, staking, stablecoin revenue and the Coinbase One subscription
moat: Regulatory licences and a security record that institutions underwrite, combined with the trust of US retail customers in a sector where many competitors have failed.
risks: Revenue rises and falls with crypto trading volumes, which are highly volatile
It reported a loss in the latest period on investment and asset write-downs
Trading fees are under pressure as competitors cut prices
Regulation of crypto in the US remains unsettled
opportunities: Revenue grew about 31% a year over three years
Analysts see large upside, with a median target well above the current price
Subscription and services revenue, including stablecoin income, grows regardless of trading volumes
watch: Trading volumes and the share of revenue from subscriptions and services.
